### Barter
**Definition:** Trading with goods directly instead of using money
**Scenario Match:** Trading a power bank directly for a box of tissues without using any money.
### Double Coincidence of Wants
**Definition:** neither of the trading partners would get what they want so no trade happens
**Scenario Match:** Failing to trade because you have cards but the other person needs tissues, and neither of you wants what the other has.
### Medium of Exchange
**Definition:** using money instead of goods to trade
**Scenario Match:** Using gold coins to buy an apple instead of having to find a specific trade partner who wants your spare staples.
### Scarcity
**Definition:** There isn't enough stuff to satisfy everyone's wants
**Scenario Match:** The fundamental problem that there wasn't enough bread printed for everyone in the room to finish their mission cards.
### Shortage
**Definition:** There is a thing that happens that slows or stops production temporarily so prices will rise
**Scenario Match:** The situation after the 'drought' where the sudden removal of wheat meant many students couldn't find any, despite having the money.
### Inflation
**Definition:** when the price of most if not all goods increases making each dollar worth less
**Scenario Match:** A general rise in prices across the room because Prof Smith injected more cash into the system.
### Deflation
**Definition:** price of most or all goods going down making each good worth less and your money is worth more
**Scenario Match:** Prices for bookmarks dropping because Prof Smith only had 29 gold coins and couldn't afford to pay the original price.
### Liquidity
**Definition:** having more money on hand to buy things, instead of physical capital like machinery or goods to sell
**Scenario Match:** Prof Smith randomly dropping extra dollar bills onto students' desks to increase the amount of cash available for trading.
### Monopoly
**Definition:** A single company controlling the supply of something so they can increase the price as much as they want
**Scenario Match:** The 'Dead' students in the graveyard being the only ones left with wheat and charging whatever they wanted because there was no competition.
### Specialization
**Definition:** One person doing one specific part of a job instead of making the whole bookmark themselves
**Scenario Match:** One student focusing only on cutting paper while another focused only on taping to increase their total output of bookmarks.
### Division of Labor
**Definition:** If you want to build a ship instead of everyone building a ship you get different people to do
**Scenario Match:** Breaking the bookmark-making process into a 'factory line' where each person performed one specific task.
### Incentives
**Definition:** When the government gives you tax break when you get a heat pump over gas heating
**Scenario Match:** Students forming 'corporations' because they realized they could earn more gold coins by working together than as individuals.
### Rational Self-Interest
**Definition:** Doing something that benefits you disregarding other peoples interests
**Scenario Match:** Students focusing solely on completing their own mission cards to 'survive,' regardless of how it impacted the rest of the market.
### The Invisible Hand
**Definition:** Prices of goods naturally changing depending on how much people are willing to pay
**Scenario Match:** Prices for bread and wheat adjusting naturally based on student demand after the drought, without Prof Smith setting a price.
### Competition
**Definition:** Many companies selling the same good competing for business, each company will lower rices and increase quality to try to get you to buy their stuff
**Scenario Match:** The 'Artisan' student producing a single high-quality bookmark while the 'Corporation' next to him produced ten faster, forcing everyone to consider price vs. quality.
